response:
---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Operating Profit Sharpe
EXPRESSION: RATIO(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3), VOL(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: A given level of operating profitability is worth more when it has been delivered with low year-to-year dispersion; smoothed ROA per unit of ROA volatility isolates durable operating strength from lucky or cyclical spikes.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The numerator is the profitability theme (three-year mean operating ROA) and the denominator is the quality theme (five-year instability of that same profitability), so the signal is scale-free "profit per unit of profit risk." Investors appear to underprice persistence, extrapolating high-volatility profits and discounting quietly stable ones, so the ratio should carry a positive slope beyond either component alone.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Cash Backed High ROA Gate
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), INDICATOR(SUB(oancf, ib), 0))
HYPOTHESIS: High reported profitability only predicts returns when it is validated by operating cash flow exceeding accrual earnings; accrual-inflated profitability is transient and mean-reverts.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The rank of EBITDA-to-assets carries the profitability theme, while the indicator that cash flow exceeds net income is a quality gate on earnings integrity. Switching the profitability rank off for non-cash-backed firms creates a genuine conditional interaction: the long leg holds only high-profit firms whose profits are cash-validated, which should raise both the FMB slope and the FF5 spread alpha relative to raw ROA.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Unlevered Profit Strength
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating profitability that is not financed by heavy debt reflects true asset productivity, whereas profitability accompanied by high leverage carries distress and refinancing risk that offsets the profitability premium.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The multiplicative form means a firm scores high only when it is simultaneously highly profitable at the asset level and conservatively financed, which is the definition of durable operating strength in the economic story. Additive combinations let leverage cancel profitability; the product forces joint satisfaction and should sharpen the long-short spread beyond a single-theme ROA or low-leverage sort.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Persistence Weighted ROA
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(ib, 0), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Current profitability is more informative about future cash flows when the firm has posted positive bottom-line income in most of the last five years, so a track record of uninterrupted profitability amplifies the value of today's high margin.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The rank of operating ROA supplies the profitability theme and the five-year count of profitable years supplies a discrete quality/persistence weight, producing a graded interaction rather than a binary screen. Firms with high current ROA but a spotty history are likely at a cyclical peak, and downweighting them should improve both cross-sectional slope reliability and portfolio stability.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Stable Margin Gross Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Gross profitability signals a real competitive advantage when the underlying gross margin is stable over time; volatile margins indicate commodity pricing or cost pass-through risk rather than pricing power.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This puts profitability on the revenue-side channel (gross profit to assets) and quality on the durability of the margin itself (five-year volatility of gross margin), a mechanism distinct from ROA volatility or cash backing. Economic moats produce simultaneously high and steady margins, and the multiplicative rank interaction targets exactly that intersection.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Leverage Discounted ROE Gap
EXPRESSION: SUB(RANK(RATIO(ib, at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(ib, ceq), RATIO(ib, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Return on equity that far exceeds return on assets is manufactured by balance-sheet leverage rather than operating skill, so asset-level profitability should be rewarded while the leverage-driven wedge between ROE and ROA should be penalized.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The first term is unlevered profitability and the second is a direct measure of how much of headline equity profitability comes from financial gearing, so the difference isolates operating quality from levered profitability. This is a sign-opposed interaction that neither theme delivers alone: two firms with identical ROE separate sharply once the leverage wedge is subtracted.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE Operating Profit Sharpe---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The "profitability per unit of profitability instability" ratio is a coherent quality-scaled profitability construct rather than a literal rediscovery, but it sits close to the published earnings-volatility/QMJ-stability literature and the raw ratio will be dominated by near-zero-denominator outliers, so it should be winsorized or rank-transformed before the FMB slope is believed.

---CRITIQUE Cash Backed High ROA Gate---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Since the 0/1 indicator dominates the [0,1] rank, the sort effectively becomes "negative-accrual firms long, all positive-accrual firms short," making this a repackaging of the Sloan accruals anomaly rather than a genuine profitability-quality interaction.

---CRITIQUE Unlevered Profit Strength---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: A rank-product of high profitability and low leverage is the textbook profitability-plus-safety composite (QMJ), offers no mechanism beyond its two well-documented components, and is trivially constructed.

---CRITIQUE Persistence Weighted ROA---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The 0–5 profitable-year count both dwarfs the [0,1] ROA rank (so the signal is mostly a coarse loss-history screen, a known effect) and saturates at 5 for most surviving firms, plus the window length is ambiguous if the panel is monthly with annual data carried forward.

---CRITIQUE Stable Margin Gross Profitability---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Pairing Novy-Marx gross profitability with the durability of the gross margin itself is an economically motivated moat proxy on a distinct (revenue-side) channel from ROA-volatility variants, though its incremental content versus the Operating Profit Sharpe proposal must be checked and the five-year window will cost coverage.

---CRITIQUE Leverage Discounted ROE Gap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The ROE–ROA wedge equals ib·(at−ceq)/(ceq·at), so it flips sign for loss-makers (rewarding highly levered unprofitable firms) and explodes for near-zero or negative book equity; absent those pathologies it reduces to roughly "ROA rank minus leverage rank," i.e., the additive twin of the Unlevered Profit Strength proposal.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Lower Envelope Durable Profitability
EXPRESSION: MIN(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))
HYPOTHESIS: Durable operating strength requires profitability to be high on both the accrual and the cash channel simultaneously; the weaker of the two three-year averages is the level of profitability a firm can actually sustain, and the market prices closer to the headline accrual number.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Replacing the 0/1 gate with a MIN operator removes the indicator-dominance problem and, critically, is not the accruals anomaly: the accruals signal is the signed difference and goes long firms with low earnings but high cash flow, whereas this lower envelope refuses to reward either channel unless the other confirms it, so cash-rich low-earnings firms score low too. Three-year averaging keeps the concept about persistent dual-channel profitability rather than one-year accrual noise, and coverage stays high because only three annual observations of standard items are required.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Distress Charged Profitability
EXPRESSION: SUB(RATIO(oiadp, at), MUL(VOL(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Leverage is only dangerous in proportion to how unstable operating profits are, so the correct haircut to reported profitability is a risk charge equal to earnings volatility scaled by the debt burden; profitability that survives this charge is genuinely durable operating strength.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This is not the QMJ profitability-plus-safety rank composite: leverage enters only multiplied by earnings volatility, so a highly levered firm with rock-steady profits is barely penalized while a moderately levered firm with swinging profits is penalized heavily, a genuine three-way interaction that neither component nor their additive combination expresses. All terms are asset-scaled and in the same units, so the subtraction is economically interpretable as expected profitability net of a default-risk charge rather than an arbitrary rank blend.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Cash Flow Range Penalized Profitability
EXPRESSION: SUB(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3), SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oancf, at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm's sustainable profitability is its average operating margin less the peak-to-trough swing in its cash generation; firms whose cash flow collapses in bad years cannot capitalize their good-year profitability, so the trough matters as much as the mean.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This removes the saturating 0-5 count and the rank/count scale mismatch: both terms are continuous asset-scaled quantities, so the subtraction is unit-consistent and no firm mass piles up at a ceiling. Economically it is a downside concept rather than a loss-history screen — the range penalty distinguishes firms with a high cash-flow floor from those whose reported profitability depends on cyclical peaks — and it differs from a symmetric volatility measure by keying on the realized worst year.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Profit Net of Debt Service Burden
EXPRESSION: SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating profitability is only free cash for shareholders after interest and near-term debt maturities are covered; the same EBITDA yield is worth far less when a large fraction of it is pre-committed to servicing and rolling debt.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This abandons the ROE−ROA wedge entirely, so there is no division by book equity and no sign flip for loss-makers or firms with negative or near-zero equity; all quantities are asset-scaled and strictly comparable. It is also not the additive twin of a leverage sort because only the serviceable portion of debt enters — interest actually paid plus debt actually maturing — so long-dated, cheaply financed leverage is treated as benign while short-dated, expensive leverage directly consumes profitability.
